_comment:clarification: The actual config will just be a single dictionary represented by spec (see example for an example).  It will not need to be prefaced with this surrounding dictionary
_comment:implementation: The user should be able to specify any number of extra key-value pairs in any section (eg: `example.flags[2].listener._comment`)

spec._comment: any keys beginning with '_' are just comments and meta to define the spec.  They will not be included in the actual config

flags.title: flag_title
flags._comment: points defaults to 1.0 when not otherwise defined

litener._buffer_default_comment: by '||' I mean concatention.  i.e. anything from STDIN, STDOUT, or STDERR

_buffer_options.implication: `listener.match` only gets tested against what the user enters (stdin)
`listener.match` only gets tested against what the terminal outputs (stdout)
`listener.match` only gets tested against what the terminal outputs to the error buffer (stderr)
`listener.match` will be tested against the specified file within the student's terminal environment

litener._comment:buffer:implementation: this file may or may not initially exist

_type_options.implication: `listener.match` will be tested against `listener.buffer`.  If a match is found, the flag will be marked as completed
_type_options.syntax: since json uses backslash to escape values, all escape sequences must be double-escaped

_type_options.implication: `listener.match` will be tested against `listener.buffer`.  The flag will only be marked as complete if they are the exact same
_type_options.comment:implementation: you may want to hash this and then just check if the file's hash matches

_type_options.implication: `listener.buffer` will be hashed with MD5 and matched against `listener.match`
_type_options.comment:priority: this is low priority.  Don't worry about doing this now, but it is something to consider for the future
restrictions: `listener.match` must be a valid MD5 hash

spec._comment:implementation: the flags should be presented in the order the appear in `flags`
